The saguaro ( / s ə ˈ ( ɡ ) w ɑːr oʊ / sə- (G)WAR -oh , [ 5 ] Spanish: [saˈɣwaɾo] ; Carnegiea gigantea ) is a tree-like cactus species in the monotypic genus Carnegiea that can grow to be over 12 meters (40 feet) tall. It is native to the Sonoran Desert in Arizona , the Mexican state of Sonora , and the Whipple Mountains and Imperial County areas of California. Saguaro typically grow at elevations ranging from sea level to 4,500 feet (1,400 m), although they may be found at up to 5,000 feet (1,500 m). [ 6 ] The saguaro blossom is the state wildflower of Arizona. Its scientific name is given in honor of Andrew Carnegie . In 1933, Saguaro National Park , near Tucson, Arizona , was designated to help protect this species and its habitat.
